{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Tamar Schlick''' is an American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] who works as a professor of chemistry, mathematics, and computer science at [[New York University]]. Her research involves developing and applying tools for modeling and simulating [[biomolecule]]s.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://monod.biomath.nyu.edu/index/people/tamar_cv/TSchlick.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Tamar Schlick|date=October 8, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170708234708/http://monod.biomath.nyu.edu/index/people/tamar_cv/TSchlick.pdf|archive-date=2017-07-08|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Schlick did her undergraduate studies at [[Wayne State University]], graduating in 1982 with a B.S. in mathematics.<ref name="cv"/> She continued her graduate studies at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at New York University, completing a Ph.D. in applied mathematics in 1987 under the supervision of [[Charles S. Peskin]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=33114}}</ref>

After postdoctoral studies at NYU and the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], she returned as a faculty member to NYU in 1989.<ref name="cv"/>

==Recognition==
She is a [[fellow]] of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2004), [[American Physical Society]] (2005), [[Biophysical Society]] (2012), and [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (2012).<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{citation|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2012|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170726172025/https://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2012|archive-date=2017-07-26|url-status=dead}}</ref>
